title: Conditions, Boolean Logic, and Boundaries
summary: Express mutually exclusive decisions with comparisons, boolean operators, if/else, switch expressions, and explicit boundary tests.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the Java behavior taught in Conditions, Boolean Logic, and Boundaries
Compile, run, and test the behavior with observable evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: `if`, `else if`, and `else` select one path according to boolean conditions. `&&` and `||` short-circuit, which can protect later operations from invalid state. Use parentheses when operator precedence is not immediately clear. Compare strings and value objects with `.equals`, using a constant on the left when null is possible. Modern switch expressions work well for finite categories and require intentional exhaustiveness. Test values below, at, and above every threshold; `score >= 60` includes 60 while `score > 60` does not.
keyPoints: `if`, `else if`, and `else` select one path according to boolean conditions.
commonMistakes: parseInt does not accept arbitrary decimal text
using non-short-circuit operators can evaluate unsafe expressions
